questions.question_text: A quiz has $9$ multiple-choice questions, each with five options and exactly one correct answer. A student guesses every answer. Find the probability that she gets at least one question correct, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Stopped at $P(X=0)$ without subtracting it from $1$.
Found $P(X=1)$, the probability of exactly one correct, instead of at least one.
Used $1-P(X \le 1)$, treating 'at least one' as 'at least two'.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(7,0.15)$. Find $P(X \le 2)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Used only the single term $P(X=2)$ instead of summing from $r=0$.
Subtracted the correct sum from $1$, giving $P(X \ge 3)$ instead of $P(X \le 2)$.
Included the extra term $P(X=3)$, so the sum ran to $r=3$.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(10,0.3)$. Find $P(X \ge 3)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Subtracted $P(X \le 3)$ instead of $P(X \le 2)$, the off-by-one on the boundary.
Found $P(X \le 2)$ and forgot to subtract it from $1$.
Used the single term $P(X=3)$ instead of the whole range from $3$ upwards.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(6,0.35)$. Find $P(X > 2)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Used $1-P(X \le 1)$, treating 'more than $2$' as 'at least $2$' and so including $X=2$.
Found $P(X \le 2)$ and forgot to subtract it from $1$.
Used the single term $P(X=3)$ instead of every value above $2$.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(8,0.4)$. Find $P(X < 3)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Found $P(X \le 3)$, including $X=3$, which the strict inequality excludes.
Used only $P(X=2)$ instead of summing every value below $3$.
Subtracted the correct sum from $1$, giving $P(X \ge 3)$.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(10,0.4)$. Find $P(4 \le X \le 6)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Started the sum at $r=3$, adding a term below the lower endpoint.
Left out $P(X=6)$, treating the upper endpoint as excluded.
Left out $P(X=4)$, treating the lower endpoint as excluded.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(15,0.2)$. Find $P(X \ge 4)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Subtracted $P(X \le 4)$ instead of $P(X \le 3)$, the off-by-one on the boundary.
Found $P(X \le 3)$ and forgot to subtract it from $1$.
Used the single term $P(X=4)$ instead of the whole range from $4$ upwards.

questions.question_text: $X \sim \text{Bin}(5,0.45)$. Find $P(X \le 2)$, correct to four decimal places.

options.why: Stopped the sum at $r=1$, leaving out $P(X=2)$ that 'at most $2$' includes.
Used only the single term $P(X=2)$ instead of summing from $r=0$.
Subtracted the correct sum from $1$, giving $P(X \ge 3)$ instead of $P(X \le 2)$.
